ACT-SC6-P1-Q1.note: M is the dash-dot/open-diamond series (label M at the right end, x=20). At 5 mg/L its marker sits one minor division above the 15-min gridline => 16 min. RESOLVABLE: comfortably. The three distractors are the 5 mg/L values of J (30), L (9) and K (21), so the read only has to separate values 5-14 min apart (11-31 px at the served 260 width); the fine 16-vs-15 distinction is never required. Every distractor is the endpoint of a real error (traced the wrong line back from the right-edge labels), which is the dominant error on this item type since J and M cross between 10 and 15 mg/L. Marker shapes disambiguate the crossing, so tracing is safe. One coincidence worth recording, not enough to drop the item: 9 + 21 = 30, leaving 16 as the only option not in that relation; a test-wise student could notice the odd-one-out. I would re-deal the numbers so no two distractors sum to a third.

ACT-SC6-P1-Q2.pick: Additive J gave its greatest clearing time of the concentrations tested
ACT-SC6-P1-Q2.note: Experiment 2 used 10 mg/L (stated in the passage, not in the stem - that is the work). At 10 mg/L: J = 47, which is J's maximum (J runs 12, 30, 47, 36, 21 and is the only series that peaks anywhere but 20 mg/L). K (12,21,27,29,33), L (12,9,8,18,27) and M (12,16,40,42,46) all rise monotonically to their maximum at 20 mg/L. RESOLVABLE: comfortably, and it does not turn on a tight read. M is the only near-call numerically (40 at 10 vs 42 at 15, a 4.4 px difference between two open diamonds) but M keeps climbing to 46 at 20, so the shape of the curve settles it without measuring the 40/42 gap. Mild option-set weakness: three of the four options are false for the identical reason (peak at 20 mg/L), so a student who spots that pattern disposes of them together - but only after reading the figure, so it is not a shortcut to the key.

ACT-SC6-P1-Q3.note: Figure 2: K unstirred 27, stirred 32 - the only pair whose open bar is taller. J 47 -> 17, L 8 -> 4, M 40 -> 36. RESOLVABLE: yes, and this is the repair working. The K bar tops differ by 11 px at the served width (5 min at 2.2 px/min), against the 2.4 px reported before the redraw; it reads as a taller white bar at native 260 with no magnification. The next-closest pairs, L and M, are 8.8 px apart and also read directly. Both bar types carry the same 1 px black stroke, so the white bar's top edge is as locatable as the black one's - confirmed in the rendered raster, not only in the source. Distractors: M is the honest near-miss (only 4 min lower, and the tallest pair on the chart), L is the other 4-min drop, J is the blowout a careless reader picks if they invert the legend.

ACT-SC6-P1-Q4.note: Two steps: Figure 2 identifies the additive (J drops 47 -> 17, i.e. 30 min; the next largest drops are L and M at 4 min each, and K rises), then Figure 1 gives J at 15 mg/L = 36. 'By far more' is unambiguous on both absolute (30 vs 4) and proportional (64% vs 50%) readings, so there is no second defense. RESOLVABLE: comfortably. Step 1 is a 66 px bar difference. Step 2 lands one minor division above the 35-min gridline; the options are 7+ min apart (18, 29, 42, 36), so the exact 36-vs-35 reading is not load-bearing. Distractors are the 15 mg/L values of L (18), K (29) and M (42) - each the endpoint of picking the wrong series in step 1 or tracing the wrong line in step 2. Best-constructed item in the set.

ACT-SC6-P1-Q5.note: K@5 = 21, K@10 = 27, so 7.5 mg/L interpolates to 24. RESOLVABLE: comfortably, and robustly - the two bracketing points are 13.2 px apart, and the answer survives a sloppy read (20 and 28 still give 24 as the closest option). Distractors: 21 is the failure to interpolate at all (reads the lower endpoint), 12 is the additive-free control at 0 mg/L, 16 is M@5, i.e. the wrong series. Not reachable without solving: no option is the sum or difference of two others, and nothing in the configuration supplies the value. Partial shortcut worth noting - the key is the only option greater than 21, so a student who reads K@5 = 21 and knows only that the curve rises can skip the midpoint arithmetic; that still requires the figure, so it does not break the item, but it means the interpolation is softer than it looks.

ACT-SC6-P1-Q6.note: The comparison standard is the additive-free mean plotted at 0 mg/L = 12 min (the passage says so, and it is drawn as a distinct larger open circle where all four series begin). L is the only additive that goes below it: 9 at 5 mg/L and 8 at 10 mg/L. J (30,47,36,21), K (21,27,29,33) and M (16,40,42,46) are above 12 at every tested concentration. RESOLVABLE: yes, but this is the tightest comparison remaining in the batch and the one I would name if anything were to be tightened further. The decisive gaps are 6.6 px (control 12 vs L@5 9) and 8.8 px (control vs L@10 8) between a filled triangle and the open control circle. What rescues it is the gridline: the control sits one minor division ABOVE the 10-min major and both L points sit below it, so the reader compares each to a printed line rather than to each other. Verified in the 260-px raster without magnification. Distractors are plausible - the natural error is comparing the curves to one another (L is lowest everywhere, J is highest at 10) or forgetting that the 0 mg/L point is the control at all.
ACT-SC6-P1-Q6.figure_read: control (0 mg/L) = 12; L = 9 at 5 and 8 at 10

_meta.leak_check: No key or difficulty leak found in the render. Fields present are id, passage_id, passage_title, format, passage, graphic, prompt, choices, domain - correct_answer, difficulty, explanation, solve, distractor_solve and subskill are all absent. domain is an ACT reporting category and does not narrow the key. Key positions after the re-deal are index 2,3,0,3,2,0 - two each in slots 1, 3 and 4 and none in slot 2, which is unremarkable at n=6. Two things the render does that are not leaks but are worth passing on: (1) the re-deal leaves numeric options unsorted (Q1 '30, 9, 16, 21'; Q4 '18, 29, 42, 36'; Q5 '12, 21, 24, 16'), whereas the real ACT orders numeric choices monotonically - the shipped order should be restored to ascending, since a scrambled numeric ballot is itself an off-exam tell; (2) Q1's distractors contain the arithmetic coincidence 9 + 21 = 30, which makes the key the odd one out.
_meta.difficulty_calibration: Against the enhanced ACT Science section (40 questions in 40 min, 6 passages), this set grades two easy and four medium, with no hard item. Every question is a locate-and-read or a two-step locate-then-read; none requires reconciling a conflict between the two experiments, extending a trend past the plotted range, or evaluating a design choice. Q6 is the closest to the section's harder end because it makes the student notice that 0 mg/L is the control rather than a data point. That is a reasonable profile for one research-summaries set and I am not calling it a failure, but if this set was commissioned to supply hard items, it does not.
